# proxy-protocol-runtime

Repository-authored, sanitized NGINX migration fixture for issue #366 (imported HTTP PROXY-protocol identity evidence, per #366's 2026-09-21 amendment). It uses only synthetic local addresses, hostnames, paths, and values; it contains no production configuration, credentials, or external endpoints.

The exact assessment contract, candidate disposition, categories, origin, and license are recorded in `manifest.json`. It reuses the `#426` `listen ... proxy_protocol;` + `real_ip_header proxy_protocol;` + `set_real_ip_from` translation and proves the resulting `[[servers]] proxy_protocol = "in"` / `[servers.client_address] trusted_proxies` runtime security boundary end to end through a real Jul instance: a real local relay bound to the one trusted source address prepends a genuine PROXY v1 header asserting an arbitrary client address, which Jul honors as the canonical client (observable in the `X-Forwarded-For` it forwards upstream); the same bytes sent from an untrusted direct peer are refused outright rather than served on a spoofed or fallback identity, per the documented "a connection from an address outside the set is refused" contract (`docs/configuration.md`).

The real-Jul E2E lives in `cmd/jul/corpus_runtime_test.go` (`TestNGINXCorpusProxyProtocolRealE2E`) rather than the generic manifest `scenarios` array, because it needs to control the raw TCP peer address (via `net.Dialer.LocalAddr`, binding to a second loopback alias to simulate a distinct trusted-vs-untrusted network position on a single test machine) and inject a raw PROXY protocol header before the HTTP request, which the generic single-request/response Scenario/Dimension model does not express.
